# SoduWork

## The AI-native engine for teams and their agents

**A chat ends with an answer. A SoduWork request ends when the person who asked signs off.**

**Multi-harness · Multi-agent · Self-hosted**

Works with Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork
cd SoduWork
```

| Platform | Start command |
| --- | --- |
| macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` |
| Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` |
| Windows Command Prompt | `start.cmd --desktop` |

[Website](https://soduwork.ai) | [Live demo](https://soduwork.ai) | [Documentation](docs/README.md) | [Docs website](https://dev.soduwork.ai) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases)
[![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#quick-start)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)

---

## What SoduWork can do for you

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **One harness does the work, another reviews it** | Pick Pi to do the work. OpenCode, on a different model, reviews it against the acceptance criteria. If the review fails, the work goes back with the reasons. |
| **Hand a request to a colleague's agent** | People and AI work together: you file a request, AI writes the acceptance criteria, and you assign it to yourself or a colleague. The assignee's agent does the work and reviews it, and a person signs off. Everyone on the request can see who did what. |
| **Turn one person's know-how into a team asset** | When you and AI get a task right, save the chat as a plugin. After review, anyone on the team can use it and contribute improvements, with access granted as needed. |

## Core ideas

**🔀 Smart dispatch**

**The right agent and model for each job.**

- Pick a harness for each step and switch mid-conversation
- Routine steps on cheap or local models, strong models where it matters
- Long tasks go to your own cloud runner

**🛡️ Built-in governance**

**Your organization decides which AI does what, and where.**

- Plugins are reviewed before they are shared, granted to teams or people, and can be revoked
- Roles, usage, cost and an audit log
- Self-hosted

**✅ Verified delivery**

**Set the bar first. Done means the requester signed off.**

- Every request carries its acceptance criteria
- A separate AI review checks each one
- A person makes the final call

## Quick start

> SoduWork is in public beta. Try it and tell us what you think, and evaluate it before using it in production.

You need Python 3.12+, Node.js 22.19+ and Git.

From the cloned repository, run `sh start.sh --desktop` on macOS/Linux, `.\start.cmd --desktop` in Windows PowerShell, or `start.cmd --desktop` in Command Prompt.

The first run installs dependencies, then starts the Hub, the admin console and the desktop client on this computer. Set a password for the `admin` account (12–128 characters) when asked. Then add a model provider under **Model catalog** in the admin console, start a chat in the client and try a small task. Pi is built in.

### Already added an API key? Start here

1. **Add a chat model as well.** Under **Capabilities → Model catalog**, find the service you connected, choose **Add model**, enter the provider's exact model ID, select **Chat model**, and save. Saving a service credential alone does not create a selectable model.
2. **Open the desktop client and sign in to the same Hub.** Use `--desktop` when starting from source. The browser admin console configures the service; check that **Connection** on the desktop sign-in screen points to that same Hub.
3. **Choose New conversation, Pi, and the model you added.** Pi uses the SoduWork model catalog. Codex uses its own account and needs its own sign-in; it does not automatically use this API key.
4. **Try a small task.** For example: “Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action table with owner and due date. Mark missing information as unconfirmed: Alex will organize the requirements by Friday; Sam will check the quotation.” Check the returned table against the notes.
5. **Create a requirement when you need assignment and acceptance.** Describe the goal, inputs and acceptance criteria, open **Arrange execution**, choose an Agent and model, and inspect the delivery before accepting it. A normal conversation does not require a project, plugin or automation first.

For the first message, use an **OpenAI-compatible chat model with Pi**. A successful connection probe does not guarantee a successful inference: balance, model permissions and protocol support still matter. If the Agent list is empty, check **Agent management** and the Runner connection. If the model list is empty, check that the model exists, is enabled, and both interfaces use the same Hub.

See [Run from source: send your first AI message](docs/getting-started.en.md#send-your-first-ai-message) for field-by-field setup and troubleshooting.

Try the live demo

Download the client from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest), enter `https://service.soduwork.ai` under **Connection** on the sign-in screen, then sign up and sign in.

> The demo is for evaluation only. Don't upload real business data or anything sensitive.

Install the desktop client

Follow the illustrated [desktop installation and first conversation guide](docs/desktop-quickstart.en.md).

| macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `SoduWork--mac-.dmg` |

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.
Point it at your app: it records what the original does, your coding agent writes the Rust one piece at a time,
and every piece is checked against that recording before it moves on. It doesn't translate code; it proves the rewrite.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  

Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · MCP Registry · Real-world ports · FAQ
Languages · How it works · Whole apps · Sponsors · MIT
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by  CodeRabbit

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical

  
  
  Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: record, replay and the front door today; unit ports come next.

  
    
      Record
      record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws.
    
    
      Port
      bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust.
    
    
      Check
      diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes.
    
    
      Lift
      When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
    
  

**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your
Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the
Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP
servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on
[napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and
[wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your
language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the
recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Whole tools
and servers, or only the slow part, one hot path at a time:

| Real project, same output as the original | Original | With rust-anything |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Prettier](docs/real-world.md#prettier) 3.6.2, 2,360 JS/TS files from the command line | 128.6 s | **6.9 s: 19x faster** |
| Prettier, 6,305 Markdown files from the command line | 352 s | **22.5 s: 15.6x faster** |
| [json-server](docs/real-world.md#json-server), a whole Node server: memory at idle | 74 MB | **3.5 MB**, one 5.3 MB binary |
| json-server, from start to first response | 79 to 85 ms | **8 to 10 ms** |
| [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) search over 50,000 strings, per query | 91.2 ms | **2.8 ms: 32x faster** |

Prettier: 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs format fully in Rust across 10 languages (JavaScript,
TypeScript, JSX, JSON, GraphQL, YAML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, Less), and all 17,224 match Prettier
byte for byte, since anything not ported yet falls back to Prettier. json-server: 514/514
recorded HTTP cases match on a pure Rust binary. Measured on an Apple M4, two runs each, every
output compared before timing ([details](docs/real-world.md)). Calling Rust once per small
function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. Against
C the win is safety, not speed: [ffmpeg's libavutil](docs/real-world.md#ffmpeg) ported to Rust
matches all 135,773 recorded calls and runs at about C's speed (15 of 34 benchmarks even, 6
faster, 13 slower by 2 to 32%).

> [!WARNING]
> `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on
> many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay`

> database or calls the network does that once per case. Run them on a copy of the project, with a

  A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE]
> **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers,
> filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil
> last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

  How it works ·

      🔍 Study anything
      Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.
    
    
      🛠️ Build your own
      Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.
    
    
      ✅ Checked, not guessed
      Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.
    
    
      🤖 Agent-ready
      320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.
    
  

## How it works

Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps,
asking you in plain words when a decision is yours:

1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs.
2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your
   request names (or a sensible default).
3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet.
4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

  
    
      
      Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
    
    
      
      Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
    
  

## Two ways to use it

- **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it,
  press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the
  agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and
  buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom.
  "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode).
- **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C,
  disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console.

Both modes drive the same engine.

## Clean room or Deep

- **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page
  source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor
  sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened)
  and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused
  and say how to turn on Deep mode.
- **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the
  built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start
  page watched, and the builder may use all of them.

Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system
sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can
read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can
refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see
[`docs/claude-code.md`](docs/claude-code.md).

Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with
`--deep` (or `--clean-room`).

  
  
  Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI

Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft
Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything
never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with
Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter
exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed
Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. **Grok Build** can use your
installed `grok` program through ACP (`grok agent stdio`): sign in separately with `grok login`.
See [docs/grok.md](docs/grok.md). Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI,
Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki, Devin) can be switched to it per backend; of those, Maki
and Devin have been run live (Devin authenticates with the backend's stored key — its own CLI
sign-in doesn't count over ACP). Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok, when `XAI_API_KEY` is
set) and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI).

## 可以做什么

DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。

- **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。
- **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。
- **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。
- **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。
- **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。
- **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。

功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。

## 安装

安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。

1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。
2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。
3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。

仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。

本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。

## 数据与权限

模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。

“发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。

DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解：

- **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。

## 常见问题

和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？

没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。

安全吗？

本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。

切到后台会被杀吗？

部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。

对手机有什么要求？

Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。

开源吗？

开源，代码就在这个仓库，以 [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) 发布，`sdk/` 和 `examples/` 为 MIT。DSH Go 的名称和标识，以及 Deepy、鲸娘两位吉祥物，不在开源授权范围内，见 [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md)。再发布和 fork 时的署名要求见[授权范围与再发布](#授权范围与再发布)。

## 从源码构建

以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。

先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git
cd dsh-go

bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh
source tooling/env.sh
flutter --version
java -version

bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon
```

工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。

产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。

构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时：

```bash
bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon
```

未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。

只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行：

```bash
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all
```

# Floorplan

**See how your app actually fits together.**

Claude or Codex reads your codebase and draws an interactive map of it. Every part, file and web request gets a plain-English name, and every connection between them is shown.

[![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-plugin-D97757?style=flat-square)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)
[![Codex plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codex-plugin-111?style=flat-square)](docs/codex.md)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/haydenschmitty/floorplan/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests)](https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.11.0-111?style=flat-square)](CHANGELOG.md)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-111?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![Node 18+](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A518-111?style=flat-square)](https://nodejs.org)
[![Zero dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-111?style=flat-square)](#how-it-works)

**[Try the live demo](https://haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo/)** · [Watch the video](https://youtu.be/NTUUzC7L_NQ) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Compared](#floorplan-archify-or-understand-anything) · [Features](#features) · [See it in action](#see-it-in-action) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [FAQ](#faq)

  

▶ Watch the walkthrough: installing Floorplan, then a tour of Brewline, a demo coffee-subscription app built across four repos.
Try the live demo → Explore the Brewline map in your browser, no install needed.

## Why Floorplan?

You built an app, probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask "what happens when someone checks out?" or "what breaks if I change this?" and the honest answer is *no idea*.

Floorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work.

- **For builders:** understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code.
- **For teams:** onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file.
- **For working with AI:** after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why.

## Floorplan, Archify or Understand Anything?

All three turn code into something you can see, and all three are worth knowing. They answer different questions:

| | **Floorplan** | **[Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** | **[Understand Anything](https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The question it answers** | How does the app I built actually work, and what should I worry about? | How do I show this clearly? | How does this big codebase work, down to the functions? |
| **Made for** | People who build with AI and don't read the code | Anyone explaining a system, a process or an idea | Developers getting to know a large codebase |
| **What you get** | A zoomable map of your whole app: parts, files and endpoints, the screens, the requests between frontend and backend (even across repos), and outside services | A polished diagram in one of 10 types (architecture, sequence, ERD…) or a one-page explainer, from a repo or just a description | A knowledge graph of every file, function and class, with layers, a business-domain view and guided tours |
| **Only here** | **Health check** (keys in code, open Supabase tables and Firebase rules, fakeable Stripe webhooks, endpoints anyone can use), **Recent work** (what your AI just changed, and why), blueprints from a PRD | 10 diagram types, image and video exports, diagrams of things that aren't code | Diff impact, a dashboard that adapts to your role, knowledge-base graphs |
| **Runs in** | Claude Code, Codex | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and more |

**Pick Floorplan** to understand and check an app you own. **Pick Archify** to draw a diagram for a doc, a talk or a decision. **Pick Understand Anything** to study a large codebase function by function.

They also work together: map your app with Floorplan, then use Archify to draw one flow for a presentation.

## Features

**🗺️ A map at every zoom**
Start with the whole app, then double-click into a part, a group of files, a file, and its endpoints. Each view shows what it's used by and what it uses.

**💬 Plain English everywhere**
"Takes card payments at checkout", not "Stripe API wrapper". Technical terms are explained on hover, and one switch shows the developer view.

**🔌 Real connections, across repos**
It follows imports, and matches each web request in your frontend to the server endpoint that answers it, even across separate repos.

**🖥️ Start from a screen**
Pick a page you know and see everything behind it: its parts, the requests it makes, the server code, the data, and outside services.

**🧭 Ask the map**
"How does a refund reach the customer's card?" comes back as an answer plus a mini-map of just the pieces involved, with a step-by-step walkthrough.

**🩺 Health check**
Catches the classic mistakes in AI-built apps: keys in the code or sent to the browser, Supabase tables anyone can read, open Firebase rules, Stripe webhooks anyone could fake, and endpoints with no sign-in. Each comes with a ready-to-paste fix. A check, not an audit.

**🟢 Recent work**
The cards your AI just changed light up green, each with a note on how the change serves what you asked for.

**⚡ Stays current, stays yours**
Updates re-read only what changed, and an open map reloads itself. Everything runs on your machine, and nothing is committed to git.

Plus guided **flows** you can request in plain words, a one-minute **Start here** tour, **Export** to send a copy to anyone as one HTML file, a layout for **phones and tablets** with drag and pinch, search, keyboard shortcuts,

* **tools:** keep the session tool runner's maxIdleMs countdown running when a session thread terminates

### Bug Fixes

* **helpers:** keep $schema out of the transformed schema description
* **streaming:** reject characters that aren't JSON in streamed tool input

  The lenient parser for streamed tool input used to skip characters and words that aren't JSON, such as a comment, and to join numbers such as `12 3`, so it could return a value that the text doesn't contain. It now rejects such text, and a stream with such tool input fails with an error, as it already did for a bad escape or a missing comma. Valid and truncated JSON parse as before.

* **tools:** bound the grep tool's search at 60s where ripgrep is missing, and keep its regex off the main thread
* **tools:** compare directory names exactly when confining file paths on Windows
* **tools:** fully resolve file tool paths that pass through a dangling symlink
* **tools:** ignore ripgrep config files in the agent toolset grep tool
* **tools:** leave symlinks that point outside /memories out of listings
* **tools:** normalize file modes of extracted skill files

  Extracted files now get `0644`, or `0755` if any execute bit is set, in `0700` directories, whatever the archive recorded. The system `tar` must accept `--no-same-owner` and `--no-same-permissions`.

* **tools:** pass over a tar or unzip inside the directories the agent toolset's file tools can write

  `setupSkills` takes `tar`, `unzip` and a helper that `tar` starts, such as `gzip`, only from the `PATH` entries outside `workdir` and `allowedRoots`, and passes over a link that leads inside them. A host whose only `tar` or `unzip` is inside those directories can no longer download skills until one is installed outside. Only when no `PATH` entry is outside them, as with a `workdir` of `/`, is all of `PATH` still searched. A `tar` or `unzip` that fails now rejects with an `AnthropicError`.

* **tools:** pass over an rg inside the directories the agent toolset's file tools can write

  `grep` passes over an `rg` that resolves to somewhere inside `workdir` or `allowedRoots`. It uses the next `rg` on `PATH`, or the built-in search when there is none. With a `workdir` that holds every `rg` on the host, such as `/`, every search is a built-in search. `rg`, and the `tar` and `unzip` that extract skills, no longer get the `ANTHROPIC_*` variables of the process, like the shell of `bash`.

* **tools:** read memory files only through the path that was validated
* **tools:** stop looking for rg, tar and unzip in the current directory
* **tools:** stop the grep tool's built-in search at a NUL byte in a file

  The built-in search of `grep` reads no further into a file once it meets a NUL byte, much as ripgrep does. A very large binary file with no line break used to end the process with an uncaught `RangeError`.
